newsitem.title: USA: US oil analyst sees better industry management.
newsitem.headline: US oil analyst sees better industry management.

text.p: The oil industry as a whole is better managed than it has been in years, according to Frederick Leuffer, senior managing director of Bear, Stearns and Co.
Leuffer added he foresaw companies more focused on further alliances and mergers in the coming months.

"Mergers and acquisitions are a logical next step for the industry," Leuffer said. He noted that it may even be wiser for companies to look at making alliances rather than purchases in order to accentuate each company's strengths.

Leuffer pointed out recent moves by oil majors to combine operations, notably Mobil Corp and British Petroleum merging European downstream operations and Amoco and Shell Oil Co combining efforts in the Permian Basin.

Leuffer said he thought the refining and marketing sector would be "a less lousy business" in the coming years, adding that many of the factors between 1988 and 1995 which depressed margins have been absorbed.

Some of those factors for extremely weak refining and marketing returns were low gasoline demand between 1989 and 1991, debottlenecking of capacity, and the addition of new blending components for environmental regulation.
Leuffer forecast U.S. gasoline demand will grow at least two percent annually for the next four years.
